# Temple Scroll Column 35 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** 11QT (Cave 11), Col. 35 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**35:1** And no one who is unclean from any human uncleanness shall enter My temple until he purifies himself.

**35:2** And no man in whom there is a discharge, or who has had an emission of seed, shall enter My temple.

**35:3** Until the day he washes with water and the sun has set — then he may enter on the following day.

**35:4** And no blind man shall enter it all his days, so that he does not defile My temple — for I dwell in its midst.

**35:5** And no lame man, and no man in whom there is a permanent blemish — they shall not enter to defile My temple.

**35:6** And you shall warn all the sons of Israel about every uncleanness, so that they do not defile My temple.

**35:7** And every man who purifies himself from his discharge — he shall count seven days for his purification.

**35:8** And on the eighth day he shall wash his garments and bathe his whole body in living water; and he shall be clean.

**35:9** And after he is clean he may eat of the holy things; for the holy things are his food.

**35:10** And any man who has not yet completed his days of purification — he shall not eat of the holy things.

**35:11** And he shall not enter My sanctuary until his days of purification are fulfilled.

**35:12** So that the sons of Israel do not make themselves unclean in the midst of their uncleanness and defile My temple in which I dwell.

**35:13** And any man who lies with his wife and has an emission of seed — he shall not enter any part of the temple city for three days.

**35:14** And no man who is unclean shall be seen in any part of My temple.

**35:15** And you shall set watchmen at the gates of My temple to prevent any unclean person from entering it.

**35:16** For My temple is holy, and the place where I set My name is holy; and it shall not be defiled.

---

*EMET notes: Column 35 defines purity requirements for temple access. The exclusion of the blind and lame (v. 4-5) parallels 2 Samuel 5:8 and goes beyond Pentateuchal law. "Living water" (mayim chayyim) denotes flowing water. The three-day exclusion after sexual intercourse (v. 13) is stricter than Leviticus 15:18.*
